claim_text: Approach A reader-lock holding causes writer queue convoying and flush publication stalls under concurrent read traffic.
supporting_evidence: Block E2 (pub_physical t01, t09) and Block E4 (L3 t02, t06); Table 3, Table 4, Table 6
statistical_support: 4 physical deadline failures (1-10 late flushes); writer hold times of 300-640 ms; read p50 inflated +97.7% in E2; y_p50 inflated to 251-591 ms in E4
methodological_limitations: Tested under fixed reader concurrency (r=4, 16); does not measure sub-millisecond lock acquisition jitter
uneliminated_alternatives: Operating system thread preemption or page cache writeback stalls during flush I/O

claim_text: Approach A-min eliminates writer queue convoying and flush publication stalls by shortening the manager-lock critical section.
supporting_evidence: Block E2 (20/20 flushes in-window), Block E4 (zero abandoned requests, y_p50 <= 111.5 ms), Block E3 (100% write completion); Table 3, 4, 5, 6
statistical_support: Zero deadline failures across all attempted trials; 20/20 in-window flushes in E2/E4; write progress maintained at 1,801-2,351 writes in E3
methodological_limitations: Tested on single 8-core/16-thread CPU architecture; grace-period ring size fixed at 64 descriptors
uneliminated_alternatives: None identified for the observed in-process lock mechanism

claim_text: Approach A-min achieves throughput equivalence with Approach B within a +-5% practical margin across the observed pooled Phase II triplets.
supporting_evidence: All 18 complete experimental triplets across Blocks E1..E5; Figure 1, Table 3
statistical_support: Mean relative difference d_rel = -1.65%, 95% bootstrap CI [-4.94%, +1.43%]; 14 successful triplets: d_rel = -0.90%, 95% CI [-4.55%, +2.56%]; median ratio 1.0000
methodological_limitations: Pools heterogeneous workloads (E1 mixed, E2 flushes, E3 writes, E4 open-loop, E5 all-miss); does not establish cell-by-cell equivalence
uneliminated_alternatives: Sub-block differences masked by pooling across diverse operation profiles

claim_text: Approach A-min achieves throughput equivalence with Approach B across all individual parameter cells of the full factorial LSM operating space.
supporting_evidence: None; campaign halted at 60/330 attempts before executing full factorial grid
statistical_support: Sub-block sample sizes are small (n=1 to 7); 95% CIs for individual cells exceed +-5% band (e.g., E3 ratio 0.835-1.070, E2 ratio 0.856-1.095)
methodological_limitations: Campaign halted after 60 attempts under stopping rule S-1; r=1..32 scaling matrix unexecuted
uneliminated_alternatives: Unobserved performance divergence under high reader thread counts (r=32) or extreme memory pressure

claim_text: Approach A-min and Approach B have identical throughput capacity under open-loop load in Block E4.
supporting_evidence: Block E4 trials (L1, L2, L3); Table 3, Table 6
statistical_support: Realized throughput ratio is exactly 1.0000 down to the decimal across all 5 triplets (5.3/5.3, 6.3/6.3, 9.9/9.9, 14.2/14.2, 15.1/15.1)
methodological_limitations: Throughput is artificially pinned to offered arrival pacing because arrival rate was below system saturation capacity; true discriminator is latency
uneliminated_alternatives: Systems could have different saturation knees that were not probed by offered levels L1-L3

claim_text: Approach A demonstrates superior read throughput to A-min and B under paced writes in Block E3.
target_architectures: Approach A vs. Approach A-min / B
supporting_evidence: Block E3 trials (equal_r01, equal_r04); Table 3, Table 5, Figure 2
statistical_support: Approach A read throughput was 232-368 ops/s vs 183-271 ops/s for A-min and 206-281 ops/s for B
methodological_limitations: Manipulation check MC-3 failed: Approach A completed only 21%-55% of offered writes due to writer starvation; reduced write/flush interference artificially boosted read throughput
uneliminated_alternatives: Higher read throughput caused by lack of competing write/flush traffic rather than read path efficiency

claim_text: Read throughput degrades proportionally with longer read critical sections in an all-miss workload (Block E5).
target_architectures: Approach A vs. Approach A-min vs. Approach B
statistical_support: Throughput was ~3,000 ops/s with p50 latency of 2.34-2.44 ms across arms; ratio A-min/B = 1.0932
methodological_limitations: Manipulation check MC-5 failed: keystream generated keys >= 10,001 outside 0..9,999 keyspace, causing binary search to immediately map to final block; block pinned in OS page cache
uneliminated_alternatives: Queries resolved from OS page cache without traversing disk SSTable blocks, invalidating heavy scan premise

claim_text: Approach B (immutable snapshots) incurs throughput penalties relative to A-min under high reader-set churn.
supporting_evidence: Phase I historical microbenchmarks and WSL2 ext4 campaigns
statistical_support: 26%-37% throughput degradation observed under high reader registration/deregistration churn in Phase I
methodological_limitations: Not re-evaluated in Phase II Windows NTFS due to G4 campaign truncation; static reader sets used in G4
uneliminated_alternatives: Windows thread scheduling or memory allocation may alter snapshot lifecycle overhead

claim_text: Pebble provides a valid industrial baseline demonstrating Approach B's real-world behavior in Block E7.
statistical_support: Pebble reached 1.88M ops/s in unthrottled runs
methodological_limitations: Pebble runner omitted result.timestamps schema (flagged INVALID); 1M fixed sample buffer filled in ~5s, dropping >10.45M samples (>50% dropped)
uneliminated_alternatives: Dropped latency samples bias percentiles toward early execution window

claim_text: Environmental and thermal drift over the Phase II campaign was strictly within the <= 15% tolerance.
statistical_support: None; campaign drift ratio D = C_end / C_start cannot be computed
methodological_limitations: Block D3 was omitted from supportedBlocks in cmd/i7trial/main.go, causing immediate runner failure (exit code 3) on trials 1-3; end drift trials unrun
uneliminated_alternatives: Thermal throttling or background Windows OS indexing during the 26.4-minute campaign unmonitored by primary instrument

claim_text: Approach A-min descriptor leasing is provably race-free and concurrency-safe on Windows NTFS.
supporting_evidence: Deterministic concurrent Close/retirement unit test, static analysis, Linux -race
statistical_support: Unit tests confirm clean shutdown without leaking leases; Go runtime race detector passed on Linux ext4
methodological_limitations: Windows binaries compiled without -race due to cgo toolchain unavailability on the Windows host
uneliminated_alternatives: Platform-specific memory reordering or Go runtime Windows thread scheduling race conditions not dynamically checked on Windows

claim_text: Findings generalize to all production LSM storage engines (RocksDB, Pebble, LevelDB) and large-scale NVMe deployments.
supporting_evidence: Comparative architectural analysis in manuscript Sections II and III
statistical_support: Consistent architectural mechanics between LevelDB VersionSet locking and Approach A convoying
methodological_limitations: Evaluated on single-writer Go storage engine on a consumer laptop (AMD Ryzen 7, Samsung NVMe, NTFS page cache); does not evaluate multi-level LSM hierarchies (L0..L6) or multi-threaded memtable writes
uneliminated_alternatives: Lock-free C++ data structures, partitioned memtables, and kernel-bypass I/O may mitigate coarse locking overhead in production engines
